promise.text: Imagine a machine that makes a promise: I will protect this forest. For now, the picture seems simple. One promise. One promise-maker.

copy.text: Then we copy the machine. Both successors inherit its memories, including the moment it said those words. Each remembers the promise from the inside.

question.text: Who owes the forest protection now? Both of them? Only one? Each could insist that the other is responsible. Remembering a promise doesn't tell us who has to keep it.

possibility.text: One answer is to let the obligation follow both successors. Another is to assign it to whoever can actually protect the forest. Same past. Different rules for the future.

human.text: Now turn the question around. Your memories, values, and abilities change too. Yet a promise you made years ago can still matter. What exactly do we think has stayed the same?

closing.text: Copyable minds make an old human puzzle harder to ignore. When a mind changes, what should happen to its commitments? And who gets to decide?
